facts.t: Appears in 1.96% of the 42,331 paintings in our archive (831 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 428).
In our 42,331-painting archive it is more common than 71% of the named colors.
Peaks in the 1900s: found in 2.2% of the 3,193 paintings we have from then (69 paintings). Against the same museums' baseline that is 2.1x the expected rate.
Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color (41% of the 428 paintings, by lightness rank within each painting, so varnish cannot fake it).
Most devoted painter: Paul Cézanne, in 8 of 50 works here (6.4x the baseline of the museums those works come from; as photographed 5.0x; n=8).

First seen in our archive in 1300 (commons-Q18542546); the third-earliest painting is 1375, and the latest 1950 (612 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first.
Shares canvases with Dusky Blue-Green and Gnaphalium Green more than chance (lift 10.6 and 9.7; n=34 and 64).
In printed English the word peaks in the 2000s and rose fastest in the 1920s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
